text:
The largest crypto hack on record had a smaller market impact than the headline suggests.

Last week's Binance exploit was $6.3bn. Roughly $2.8bn of the stolen assets were frozen quickly by Circle, Tether and other issuers. That was possible because on-chain activity is transparent: funds can be traced, and issuers can act on what they see.

For allocators, the useful question is not whether an incident like this will recur. It is how quickly exposure can be identified, and how far it reaches. Our own check came back clean: Re7 curated vaults had no exposure to the event, across all chains and platforms.

This is the case for treating risk in layers: chain, protocol and asset. We set out that framework with Clear Street in a recent report.

The full note is in this week's Weekly: [link]
